title: Chinese Juniper: Ancient Chinese Junipers You Can Visit
meta_description: A twisting evergreen kept beside temples and palaces for centuries. Nanjing's Six-Dynasty Juniper is reckoned at about 1,500 years old.
intro: The Chinese juniper is best known in the West as a bonsai subject, trained small in a tray. Left alone for centuries beside a temple or a palace, it does the opposite: it grows into a slow, twisting giant whose bark spirals hard enough that people read dragons into it. Court records describe the coiled eastern branch at Seoul's Changdeokgung as a dragon ascending to heaven, and Beijing's Nine Dragon Cypress is a juniper misnamed by generations who never doubted the resemblance. The oldest, in Nanjing, is reckoned at about 1,500 years and is still called a pine. Kamakura's pair at Kenchoji have stood since the temple's founding in 1253, on a site once known as Hell Valley. Courts and monasteries protected what everyone else would have shaped smaller, which is why the old ones are almost all on sacred or royal ground.
